body_html:
How to think about it

Newton's law of universal gravitation: F = Gm₁m₂ ÷ r², with G = 6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg². The gravitational field strength at a distance r from a planet is g = GM ÷ r²; at Earth's surface it is 9.8 N/kg.

For a satellite in a circular orbit, gravity supplies the centripetal force: GMm ÷ r² = mv² ÷ r, so v = √(GM ÷ r). Higher orbits are slower and have longer periods (Kepler's third law). A geostationary satellite has a period of 24 h.

Example

The distance between two masses triples. What happens to the force?

Inverse square

Answer: it becomes 1/9

Example

Do higher satellites move faster or slower?

v = √(GM ÷ r)

Answer: slower

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to square r.
  • Using the height above the surface instead of the distance from the center.
  • Thinking astronauts float because there is no gravity.
